keyFindings.description: Introduced by 7efbd8af. answer now skips a revoked entry, so a revoked socket's own token, read before the revoke took effect and answered after it, takes the live socket's entry; the revoked socket's ServeHTTP then removes its unanswered entry, and the live socket's token finds none waiting and is answered read-only for the life of its socket. The mirror of N1: matching by key alone cannot tell whose token it is. Fix: give the token answer the socket's identity; the ygo fork's OnTokenAuth(room, token) gets a hook with the request (or its context), so authorizeSchemaVersion answers the connectionState's own admission, and the revoked-entry ordering goes. Add the mirror order (newer then older, revoke, the revoked socket's answer, remove newer, the live socket's answer must be writable) as a test that fails first.
'A hold takeHold just took is 13 s old at most' should read 'has at most 13 s left'.
